# Fixed Asset Accounting

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. The fixed asset register feeds depreciation, impairment and disposal results directly into the statements: capitalizing an expense inflates assets and profit, a missed impairment overstates both, there is a real risk of loss in any reporting decision taken from a dirty register, and no output here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the fixed asset accounting skill of GAJETOso/financeskills. Use it for property, plant and equipment and intangibles across the whole life cycle: acquisitions, self-construction in progress, subsequent expenditure, disposals and retirements, impairment indicators, and plain register maintenance. The capitalization decision is spelled out line by line: capitalize the purchase price plus directly attributable costs to bring the asset to working condition (delivery, installation, testing, professional fees, irrecoverable taxes) plus the initial restoration estimate and borrowing costs on qualifying assets, and expense training, relocation, administrative overhead, abnormal waste and repairs; subsequent expenditure is capitalized only when it enhances future benefits beyond the original standard. Depreciation covers the straight-line, reducing balance and units of production methods, starts when the asset is available for use rather than when it is used, stops at derecognition or held for sale classification, and applies componentization...
